title: repository.bootstrap discloses its receipt to the caller, so a partial GitHub failure is visible
description:
SPUN OUT BY worker-caece97b FROM task-80322112a48d44c69c6c55f846f8d43f (child 3, the browser form and proof row) at its step 1, 2026-09-06. That row is BLOCKED on this one. The capability belongs to the command edge landed by task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9 (DONE), which this row extends; row rail 3 on the consumer forbids it patching across the seam.

THE DEFECT, MEASURED AT HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04), six links, every one read from production source:

1. apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-service.ts:63-67 - when the GitHub half fails, `bootstrapRepository` returns `outcome: "BOOTSTRAPPED"` with `githubRefusal` set. The COMMAND SUCCEEDS. This is correct and deliberate: the local repository is real, committed and bound. It is a PARTIAL SUCCESS.
2. apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts, last line of `createRepositoryBootstrapHandler` - `return decisionOf(committed)`.
3. apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-dispatch.ts:139-144 - `decisionOf` returns exactly `{commandId, disposition, effectId, resultCode}`. The receipt is DROPPED here.
4. apps/daemon/src/http/http-adapter.ts:72-77 - `answer()` on ACCEPTED serves `{decision, httpStatus, ok, outcome}`. Still no receipt.
5. NO READ ROUTE PROJECTS IT. `git grep -rn "RepositoryBootstrapped\|REPOSITORY_BOOTSTRAPPED_EVENT" -- apps/daemon/src apps/control-room/src` excluding tests returns TWO hits, both in the writer (repository-bootstrap-command.ts:43 and :108). `/repository/remote/read` folds the PUBLISH ledger (`readProjectRemote` from repository/publish-ledger.js) which a bootstrap never writes, so it reads unbound after every bootstrap.
6. THE EVENT STREAM CARRIES NO PAYLOAD. apps/daemon/src/http/event-stream-contract.ts:154-163 `WireEvent` = {aggregateId, committedAt, eventId, eventType, globalPosition, identity, ledgerObservation, seamObservation}. apps/control-room/src/live/live-event-feed.ts:110-124 `rowOf` decodes exactly those. No payload field exists on either side.

CONSEQUENCE: `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE` is unreachable from the browser by ANY route. A caller that asked for a GitHub repository and did not get one is told plain success. That is the exact harm child 3 exists to prevent, inverted: instead of an operator deleting a good local repository because they were told "bootstrap failed", an operator believes their code is on GitHub when it is not.

The three hard refusals are NOT affected and DO reach the caller: BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY, BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE and BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN take the `receipt.outcome === "REFUSED"` branch and `throw refusalOf(receipt.refusal)`, arriving as `code @ layer`. Only the PARTIAL path is dark.

SHAPE OF THE FIX IS THE ARCHITECT'S CALL, not prescribed here. Two candidates were measured as viable: (a) widen the accepted answer so the async entry can attach a disclosure to its DurableDecision - note this touches a shape four mirrors pin, so the epic rail 1 census applies; (b) add a bootstrap-receipt read route beside the other `/*/read` routes and proxy it in apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts. (b) is the smaller blast radius and matches how every other operator card reads a daemon fact.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN: the consumer inferring the refusal from the absence of a remote. That invents an authority the daemon never stated and is what epic rail 4 and global rail 4 forbid. The code must travel VERBATIM from the layer that produced it.
definitionOfDone: A browser caller that requested a GitHub repository and did not get one can read `BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE` VERBATIM, together with its `BootstrapDetail`, over an authenticated route the control-room may proxy. Asserted by a daemon test that drives the real command edge with an injected failing `BootstrapGhPort` and reads the code back through the same seam a browser would use - not by reading the receipt object in-process.

The LOCAL half is disclosed as intact on that same path: the committed sha and the bound directory are readable, so a consumer can render 'the repository exists and is bound' without inferring it. Assert the sha matches `git rev-parse HEAD` in the created directory, read from git and not from the response.

The three hard refusals are UNCHANGED and still arrive as `code @ layer`: BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY, BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE, BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN. One arm per code, each asserting the specific code and the layer that refused, and each proven red by mutating the production surface.

NO SECRET ON THE NEW PATH. `BootstrapDetail` stays a closed literal union; no exception message, no stdout, no remote URL with embedded userinfo and no credential may reach a caller. Assert the response over the GITHUB-REQUESTED path contains no token-shaped value and no userinfo-bearing URL (epic rail 3).

If the fix adds a route: it is registered in the production listener AND in apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts, with a bidirectional roster arm (every advertised path served, every served path advertised - global rail 9). If the fix widens a returned shape: the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors are re-censused with a full-tree `git grep` of the literal and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` is run (epic rail 1).
Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. An exit-0 leg with no `Test Files N passed` line ran nothing.
taskRails: THE CODE TRAVELS VERBATIM FROM THE LAYER THAT PRODUCED IT. A consumer inferring BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE from a missing remote is inventing authority - the thing this row exists to make unnecessary.

A PARTIAL SUCCESS STAYS A SUCCESS. Do not turn the GitHub failure into a command refusal: the local repository is real, committed and bound, and refusing would tell an operator to throw it away. Disclose, do not re-classify.
NO SECRET ON ANY PATH: no credential, no stdout, no remote URL carrying userinfo. BootstrapDetail stays a closed union.

If this widens a shape the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors pin, re-census ALL FOUR with a full-tree git grep and run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` - two mirrors are invisible to `pnpm test` and the daemon leg (epic rail 1).

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE THE SEAM BEFORE BUILDING ON IT. This step EDITS NOTHING — it produces three recorded measurements, each quoted verbatim in the step note.

(1) PROVE `stateOf` RETURNS THE RECEIPT. Write an out-of-tree probe (scratchpad, `.mjs`, importing the daemon's modules by their `.js` specifiers) that opens a temp SqliteEventStore, drives a real `repository.bootstrap` through the registered command edge with an injected `BootstrapGhPort` whose `create` THROWS, then calls `stateOf(readDurableLedger(store, projectId), `${projectId}-bootstrap`)` and prints the parsed value. ASSERT IN THE NOTE that the printed object has `outcome: "BOOTSTRAPPED"`, `refusal: null`, a 40-hex `sha`, and `githubRefusal.code === "BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE"` with `githubRefusal.detail === "GH_EXECUTION_FAILED"`. Paste the probe's FULL SOURCE into the step note before deleting it — a deleted probe's transcript is a lead, not evidence (global rail 12).

IF THE VALUE IS NOT THE RECEIPT — for example if `decodeResult` yields reducer state instead — STOP AND `moe.report_blocked`. Every later step rests on this one fact and is void without it.

(2) RE-CENSUS THE DIGEST MIRRORS so DoD 5's second clause is answered rather than skipped. Run `git grep -n 'GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST' -- packages apps tools docs` and `grep -n '"/[a-z]' packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts packages/control-room-client/src/contract-pins.ts`. The architect measured the latter as ZERO hits (the generated client enumerates no route paths), which is why this shape does not widen a pinned surface. Confirm it still holds at your HEAD; if the generated client HAS gained a route roster, stop and report rather than proceed.

(3) BASELINE THE GATES AT YOUR MERGE-BASE so a later red is attributable (global rail 3). Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and `pnpm typecheck` BEFORE any edit; record each failing path with its exact lines and each `Test Files N passed` count line. Give the daemon leg its own standalone foreground call at the maximum timeout — it has measured at 560–2006s.

ADD THE READER: `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-read.ts` plus its `.js` bridge (`export * from "./repository-bootstrap-read.ts";`, matching every sibling in this directory).

EXPORT ONE FUNCTION: `readBootstrapReceipt(store: SqliteEventStore, projectId: string): BootstrapReadView`. It does exactly three things — reads `stateOf(readDurableLedger(store, projectId), `${projectId}-bootstrap`)`, PROJECTS the JsonValue into a closed literal shape, answers.

THE ANSWER SHAPE, closed and frozen: `{ outcome: "BOOTSTRAP_READ", receipt: BootstrapReceiptView | null }`, where `BootstrapReceiptView` carries EXACTLY the eight receipt keys — `version, decidedAt, dir, outcome, sha, remoteUrl, refusal, githubRefusal` — and each refusal carries EXACTLY `{code, detail, refusedBy}`.

THE PROJECTION IS A COPY, NEVER A PASS-THROUGH. Build the answer key by key from the decoded value. Do not spread the stored object, do not `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(state))` it, do not forward it. This is what makes DoD 4 STRUCTURAL rather than merely asserted: a key outside the roster cannot reach a caller because nothing copies it, so a future writer that puts a token, a stdout capture or a userinfo-bearing URL on the receipt cannot leak it through this route.

VALIDATION IS FAIL-CLOSED. `version` must equal `BOOTSTRAP_RECEIPT_VERSION`; `outcome` must be `"BOOTSTRAPPED"` or `"REFUSED"`; the outcome/sha/remoteUrl/refusal null-pairing of `BootstrapReceiptV1` (contracts.ts:40-45) must hold; every `code` must be in the local BootstrapCode roster and every `detail` in the local BootstrapDetail roster. Any failure returns `{ outcome: "BOOTSTRAP_READ", receipt: null, unreadable: true }` — never a partially-copied receipt, never the raw value. Aggregate ABSENT (no bootstrap yet) returns `receipt: null` WITHOUT `unreadable`, so "never bootstrapped" and "stored something I cannot vouch for" stay distinguishable by a caller.

PIN BOTH RUNTIME ROSTERS TO THEIR TYPE UNIONS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, at compile time, because `BootstrapCode` and `BootstrapDetail` are type-only (contracts.ts:14-24) with no runtime roster to import. For each, declare the frozen literal array then pin it both ways so `pnpm typecheck` reds on drift:
  `type RosteredDetail = (typeof DETAIL_ROSTER)[number];`
  `const _detailForward: BootstrapDetail extends RosteredDetail ? true : never = true;`
  `const _detailBackward: RosteredDetail extends BootstrapDetail ? true : never = true;`
A one-directional pin is the exact hole global rail 9 names — a subset check stays green while a served value silently vanishes from the advertised set. Comment WHY both directions exist so a later reader does not delete one as redundant.

Target under 250 physical lines. No process spawn, no filesystem access, no logging, no stringification of the request or of the stored value.

implementationPlan.description:
THE DISCLOSURE TEST — new file `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-disclosure.test.ts`. It drives the REAL command edge against a REAL listener and reads the code back over HTTP. Do not read the receipt object in-process anywhere in this file: DoD 1 rules that out explicitly, and `repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts:178`'s `committedReceipt` helper is precisely the in-process shortcut it forbids. Model the harness on that journey file's `harness`/`registerProject`/`bootstrap` helpers (:113-177) and on `http/activation-read.test.ts:169`'s `start()` for the listener half.

ARMS, each asserting a specific value and never merely a truthy one:

(A) THE PARTIAL PATH, DoD 1 — the row's reason to exist. Bootstrap WITH a `github` request and an injected `BootstrapGhPort` whose `create` THROWS. Assert the command answers ok/ACCEPTED. Then POST `/repository/bootstrap/read` with the same credential and assert `receipt.githubRefusal.code === "BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE"`, `receipt.githubRefusal.detail === "GH_EXECUTION_FAILED"`, `receipt.githubRefusal.refusedBy === "DAEMON_INGRESS"`. Code, detail and layer, all three, verbatim from the layer that produced them.

(B) THE DETAIL TRAVELS, IT IS NOT A CONSTANT. Repeat (A) with a `gh` port that RESOLVES a NON-CANONICAL `remoteUrl` — `repository-bootstrap-service.ts:27-29` rejects any URL that is not exactly `https://github.com/{owner}/{name}` — and assert the read answers detail `REMOTE_URL_REJECTED`: same code, DIFFERENT detail. Without this arm a projector that hard-coded one detail string would pass (A).

(C) A PARTIAL SUCCESS STAYS A SUCCESS — task rail 2. On the SAME read as (A), assert `receipt.outcome === "BOOTSTRAPPED"` and `receipt.refusal === null`. The command must not have been re-classified into a refusal.

(D) THE LOCAL HALF IS DISCLOSED AS INTACT — DoD 2. On the same read, assert `receipt.dir` is the created directory and `receipt.sha` EQUALS the output of `git rev-parse HEAD` executed in that directory. Read the sha FROM GIT — never compare the response to itself.

(E) NO SECRET ON THE PATH — DoD 4 and epic rail 3. `JSON.stringify` the whole GitHub-requested response and assert it matches NEITHER a token shape (`/gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/`, `/github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}/`) NOR a userinfo-bearing URL (`/:\/\/[^/@\s"]+@/`). Then a POSITIVE CONTROL so the arm cannot be vacuous: run the same three regexes over literal strings that DO contain each shape and assert they match. A pair of negative assertions with no positive control is one typo away from proving nothing.

(F) THE PRODUCTION WIRING SUPPLIES THE OPTIONAL METHOD — risk B. Call `createRepositoryWorkflowWiring({...})` and assert `typeof wiring.repositoryWorkflows().readBootstrap === "function"`. This is the arm that stops the optional port method being dead in production while every other arm passes against a hand-built port.

(G) THE ROUTE'S OWN REFUSAL PATHS, one arm per code: a session lacking `CAPABILITIES.GOAL` -> `REPOSITORY_WORKFLOW_READ_CAPABILITY_DENIED`; a principal whose projectId differs from `boundProjectId` -> `REPOSITORY_WORKFLOW_READ_PROJECT_MISMATCH`; a non-empty body -> `REPOSITORY_BOOTSTRAP_READ_REQUEST_INVALID`; a port without `readBootstrap` -> `REPOSITORY_BOOTSTRAP_READ_UNAVAILABLE`. Each asserts the CODE and the LAYER, never merely that the call refused — a second refusal layer answering first would leave a code-blind arm green while its subject rotted (global rail 1).

(H) NEVER-BOOTSTRAPPED IS NOT UNREADABLE. Read on a project with a committed `project.register` and no bootstrap: assert `receipt === null` and that the `unreadable` marker is ABSENT. Then store a malformed value on the bootstrap aggregate and assert `receipt === null` WITH `unreadable: true`. The two must be distinguishable.

RESOURCE DISCIPLINE, epic rail 4: every listener started is closed and every temp directory removed on EVERY exit path including the failing ones — in `afterEach`, not as a trailing statement. A leaked port or directory makes every later gate on this board inadmissible.

implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILL — prove every failure-path arm actually fails when the production surface is broken. An arm never seen red is a claim, not a test.

BEFORE MUTATING ANYTHING: run `git status --porcelain` on the exact paths you will touch and RECORD the output. `repository/repository-bootstrap-read.ts`, its `.js` bridge and `repository-bootstrap-disclosure.test.ts` are UNTRACKED (`??`). For every untracked path, copy it to an out-of-tree backup under %TEMP% suffixed with your worker id. `git diff -- <untracked path>` IS EMPTY BEFORE, DURING AND AFTER A MUTATION and certifies nothing — a silently unrestored mutation would ride into the commit wearing a clean diff, with the arms green because the mutation is what they were re-graded against.

SEVEN MUTATIONS, each applied ALONE, the named arm confirmed RED, then restored:
1. `repository-bootstrap-read.ts` — drop `githubRefusal` from the projected key roster -> arm (A) reds.
2. `repository-bootstrap-read.ts` — hard-code the projected `detail` to `"GH_EXECUTION_FAILED"` -> arm (B) reds while (A) stays green. This is the mutation that proves (B) earns its place.
3. `repository-bootstrap-read.ts` — copy `sha` from the wrong key -> arm (D) reds.
4. `repository-workflow-read.ts` — delete the `CAPABILITIES.GOAL` check -> the capability arm of (G) reds.
5. `daemon-repository-workflow-wiring.ts` — remove `readBootstrap` from the port literal -> arm (F) reds AND the UNAVAILABLE arm of (G) goes green for the WRONG reason; record both observations.
6. `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-service.ts:63-67` — change the partial-success return to `outcome: "REFUSED"` -> arm (C) reds. THIS PATH IS MUTATED AND RESTORED, NEVER DELIVERED CHANGED; it is deliberately not an owned file of this row.
7. DoD 3, THE THREE HARD REFUSALS, mutated in the PRODUCTION surface one at a time — `BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY`, `BOOTSTRAP_GIT_UNAVAILABLE`, `BOOTSTRAP_PROFILE_VERSION_UNKNOWN` — confirming the EXISTING arms in `apps/daemon/src/repository/repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts` (:196, :328, :307) go red. DO NOT EDIT, MOVE OR DUPLICATE THOSE ARMS: DoD 3 says UNCHANGED, this drill is how you prove they still bind after your diff, and that test file is likewise mutated-and-restored, never delivered changed.

AFTER RESTORING, prove restoration in a tool call SEPARATE from the restore itself. TRACKED paths — `git diff -- <path>` empty (this covers repository-bootstrap-service.ts, repository-bootstrap-journey.test.ts, repository-workflow-read.ts, daemon-repository-workflow-wiring.ts). UNTRACKED paths — SHA256 equality against the out-of-tree backup, computed and compared explicitly; a PowerShell copy can silently no-op and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved. Record every hash pair in the step note.
